The dative, marked by the article.

hint: Abraham names the son Sarah bore him Isaac.

notes.text: The repeated article before the participle, plain `the`.

hint: Abraham circumcises Isaac on the eighth day, as God commanded.

hint: Abraham is a hundred when Isaac is born.

notes.text: εἰμί of age, the state formula of GEN 1:2 in full, as at 17:24.

hint: Who would have told Abraham that Sarah nurses a child? For I bore a son in my old age.

[[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[I brought into the world|I brought into the world, I brought forth, I bore, I produced]] a son in the old age of me.

hint: The child grows and is weaned, and Abraham makes a great feast the day Isaac is weaned.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's ἀπογαλακτίζω, one translation, *wean from the mother's milk*: plain text, in the passive.

hint: Get up, take the child and hold him by the hand; I will make him a great nation.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts καί before it.

reading: [[stand up|stand up, rise, rise to fight against, rise to go and set out]], [[take|take, receive, take hold of and grasp and seize]] [[the young child|the young child, the slave-lad]] and [[be strong|be strong, be mighty, be powerful, rule and hold sway and be sovereign, rule among, be lord and master of and ruler over, conquer and prevail and get the upper hand, prevail and become current, prevail over, surpass and go beyond, conquer and master and outdo and surpass, become master of and get possession of, lay hold of, seize and hold fast, control and command]] [[with the hand|with the hand, with the hand and arm, with the arm]] of you it; [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] for [[a number of people accustomed to live together|a number of people accustomed to live together, a company and body of men, a host, swarms and flocks, a nation and people, the nations and gentiles, a special class, a caste and tribe, a sex]] [[big|big, great, tall, full-grown, vast and high, spacious and wide, strong and mighty, violent, loud, prevailing, weighty and important]] [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create]] him.

greek: καὶ ἀνέῳξεν ὁ θεὸς τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ εἶδεν φρέαρ ὕδατος ζῶντος καὶ ἐπορεύθη καὶ ἔπλησεν τὸν ἀσκὸν ὕδατος καὶ ἐπότισεν τὸ παιδίον.
hint: God opens her eyes; she sees a well of living water, fills the skin and gives the child a drink.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēr māyim*, *a well of water*. The Greek adds *living*.
πίμπλημι is first *to fill full of* a thing.

reading: and [[opened|opened, undid, laid open and unfolded and disclosed, got into the open sea]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[the eyes|the eyes, the sight, the dearest and best, the buds]] of her, and [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]] [[a well|a well, a tank and cistern and reservoir, an oil jar]] of water [[of living|of living, of alive, of in full life and strength, of fresh and strong]] and [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed]] and [[filled full of|filled full of, filled with, filled up, filled, filled and discharged]] [[the leathern-bag|the leathern-bag, the wine-skin, the bladder]] of water and [[gave to drink|gave to drink, watered]] [[the young child|the young child, the slave-lad]].

greek: καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετὰ τοῦ παιδίου, καὶ ηὐξήθη. καὶ κατῴκησεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, ἐγένετο δὲ τοξότης.
hint: God is with the boy; he grows, lives in the desert, and becomes an archer.

notes.lemma: ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετὰ τοῦ παιδίου
notes.text: ἦν of state, the formula of GEN 1:2 in full.
Middle Liddell is first *a bowman, archer*.

reading: and was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] [[of the young child|of the young child, of the slave-lad]], and [[was made large|was made large, was increased and augmented, was increased in power and strengthened and exalted, was promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, grew and waxed and increased, grew up]]. and [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[in the desert part|within, inside of, and by means of the desert part, the desolate, the lone and lonely and lonesome and solitary, the helpless, the reft and void and destitute, the undefended]], [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[a bowman|a bowman, archer, the Archer and Sagittarius, the city-guard]].

greek: καὶ κατῴκησεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῇ Φαραν, καὶ ἔλαβεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ γυναῖκα ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου.
hint: He lives in the desert of Paran, and his mother takes him a wife from Egypt.

notes.text: The repeated article before the name, plain `the`, as at 14:6.

reading: and [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[in the desert part|within, inside of, and by means of the desert part, the desolate, the lone and lonely and lonesome and solitary, the helpless, the reft and void and destitute, the undefended]] the [[name:Φαραν]], and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized]] for him [[the mother|the mother, the dam, the source]] [[a woman|a woman, a mistress and lady, a wife and spouse, a mortal woman]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[of earth|of earth, of land, of the ground]] [[name:Αἰγύπτου]].

names.gloss: (Φαραν, from Hebrew Pāʾrān, of uncertain meaning)
(Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ καὶ εἶπεν Αβιμελεχ καὶ Οχοζαθ ὁ νυμφαγωγὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ Φικολ ὁ ἀρχιστράτηγος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς Αβρααμ λέγων Ὁ θεὸς μετὰ σοῦ ἐν πᾶσιν, οἷς ἐὰν ποιῇς·
hint: Abimelech, with Ahuzzath his bride's escort and Phicol his army chief, says to Abraham: God is with you in all you do.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, which names Ahuzzath at 26:26.
One translation, *leader of the bride*: plain text; ἀρχιστράτηγος, LSJ, *commander-in-chief*, likewise.
δύναμις is first *power, might, strength*; *a force for war* is its third.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[in the due measure|within, inside of, and by means of the due measure, the proportion, the fitness, the vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, the advantage and profit and fruit]] [[that|that, the one there, the more remote]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] and [[name:Οχοζαθ]] the leader of the bride of him and [[name:Φικολ]] the commander-in-chief [[of the power|of the power, of the might, of the strength, of the ability, of the authority, of the force for war and forces, of the quantity, of the faculty and capacity, of the force and meaning, of the worth and value]] of him [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you [[in all|within, inside of, and by means of all, the whole, every, every single]], to which ever [[you may make|you may make, you may do, you may produce, you may create]];

names.gloss: (Αβιμελεχ, from Hebrew ʾĂbîmelek, "my father is king")
(Φικολ, from Hebrew Pîkōl, of uncertain meaning)

greek: νῦν οὖν ὄμοσόν μοι τὸν θεὸν μὴ ἀδικήσειν με μηδὲ τὸ σπέρμα μου μηδὲ τὸ ὄνομά μου, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ἣν ἐποίησα μετὰ σοῦ, ποιήσεις μετʼ ἐμοῦ καὶ τῇ γῇ, ᾗ σὺ παρῴκησας ἐν αὐτῇ.
hint: Swear to me by God that you will not wrong me or my seed or my name, but deal with me as I have with you.

notes.lemma: μηδὲ τὸ σπέρμα μου μηδὲ τὸ ὄνομά μου
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ûlnînî ûlnekdî*, *my offspring and my posterity*. The Greek has *my seed … my name*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *kaḥesed*, *according to the kindness*. The Greek has δικαιοσύνη, as at 19:19 and 20:13.
The future infinitive of ἀδικέω, whose first sense is *to do wrong*; the active's senses, as the passive took them at 16:5.
ὄμνυμι with the accusative of the one sworn by, the entry's *to swear by*.

reading: [[now|now, even now, just now]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore]] [[swear|swear, swear to and affirm and confirm by oath, swear that one will, swear by]] to me [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] not [[to do wrong|to do wrong, to do one wrong and wrong and injure, to spoil and damage]] me [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all]] [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent]] of me [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] of me, [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon]] [[the righteousness|the righteousness, the justice]], which [[I made|I fashioned, I wrought, I produced, I performed, I did]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you, [[you will make|you will make, you will do, you will produce, you will create]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] me and [[to the earth|to the land, to the dry ground, to the terrestrial realm]], to which you [[you dwelt beside|you dwelt beside, you dwelt along the coast of, you lived near, you dwelt among, you lay near, you lived in and sojourned]] in her.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Αβρααμ Ἐγὼ ὀμοῦμαι.
hint: Abraham: I will swear.

notes.text: The future of ὄμνυμι.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] I [[I will swear|I will swear, I will swear to and affirm and confirm by oath, I will swear that one will, I will swear by]].

greek: καὶ ἤλεγξεν Αβρααμ τὸν Αβιμελεχ περὶ τῶν φρεάτων τοῦ ὕδατος, ὧν ἀφείλαντο οἱ παῖδες τοῦ Αβιμελεχ.
hint: Abraham reproves Abimelech about the wells of water his servants seized.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēr hammayim*, *the well of water*, singular. The Greek has the plural.
ἐλέγχω is first *to disgrace, put to shame*; *to cross-examine, question … censure, accuse* is its second.
The middle of ἀφαιρέω, *to take away for oneself*.

reading: and [[disgraced|disgraced, put to shame, cross-examined and questioned, censured and accused, brought to the proof and disproved and confuted, brought convincing proof, proved]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very]] [[of the wells|of the wells, of the tanks and cisterns and reservoirs, of the oil jars]] of the water, of which [[took away for themselves|took away for themselves, took away, prevented and hindered from]] [[the children|the children, the sons, the daughters, the grandchildren, the boys and youths and lads, the girls and maidens, the slaves and servants and men and maids]] of [[name:Αβιμελεχ]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Αβιμελεχ Οὐκ ἔγνων, τίς ἐποίησεν τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο, οὐδὲ σύ μοι ἀπήγγειλας, οὐδὲ ἐγὼ ἤκουσα ἀλλʼ ἢ σήμερον.
hint: Abimelech: I do not know who did this; you did not tell me, and I heard only today.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἀλλά.
ἀλλά and ἤ, `otherwise` and `or`; σήμερον plain.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to him [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] not [[I learned to know|I learned to know, I perceived, I marked, I learned, I discerned and distinguished]], who [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced, performed, did]] [[that which has been done|that which has been done, the deed, the act, anything necessary and expedient, the thing of consequence and importance, the action and affair, the thing and the business]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]], [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all]] you to me [[you brought tidings|you brought tidings, you reported, you announced, you carried a report, you related and narrated]], [[but not|but not, and not, nor, not even, not at all]] I [[I heard|I heard, I had hearing of, I heard tell of, I hearkened and gave ear, I listened to and obeyed]] [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly]] [[or|or, either or, whether or, than and as, rather]] to-day.

greek: καὶ ἔλαβεν Αβρααμ πρόβατα καὶ μόσχους καὶ ἔδωκεν τῷ Αβιμελεχ, καὶ διέθεντο ἀμφότεροι διαθήκην.
hint: Abraham gives Abimelech sheep and cattle, and the two make a covenant.

notes.text: διατίθεμαι, the chain of GEN 15:18, in the plural; ἀμφότερος, *each* or *both of two*.

reading: and [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[things that walk forward|things that walk forward, cattle, flocks and herds, horses, small cattle, sheep]] and [[calves|calves, young bulls, heifers and young cows, boys and girls and maids, young animals]] and [[gave|gave, granted, provided, gave over and delivered up]] to [[name:Αβιμελεχ]], and [[arranged as they liked|arranged as they liked, disposed of, disposed of their property and devised it by will, set out for sale and disposed of, arranged mutually, made a covenant with, settled with]] [[each|each, both of two]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant]].

greek: καὶ ἔστησεν Αβρααμ ἑπτὰ ἀμνάδας προβάτων μόνας.
hint: Abraham sets seven ewe lambs of the flock apart.

notes.text: ἀμνάς, one translation, *a lamb*: plain text.
μόνος, the chain of GEN 2:18.

reading: and [[made to stand|made to stand, set, stopped and stayed and checked, set up and raised, established and instituted, appointed, weighed]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] seven lambs [[of anything that walks forward|of anything that walks forward, of cattle, of flocks and herds, of horses, of small cattle, of sheep]] [[alone|alone, left alone, forsaken and solitary, only]].

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Αβιμελεχ τῷ Αβρααμ Τί εἰσιν αἱ ἑπτὰ ἀμνάδες τῶν προβάτων τούτων, ἃς ἔστησας μόνας;
hint: What are these seven lambs you have set apart?

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] to [[name:Αβρααμ]] what are the seven lambs [[of anything that walks forward|of anything that walks forward, of cattle, of flocks and herds, of horses, of small cattle, of sheep]] [[of these|of these, of the nearer, of what follows]], which [[you made to stand|you made to stand, you set, you stopped and stayed and checked, you set up and raised, you established and instituted, you appointed, you weighed]] [[alone|alone, left alone, forsaken and solitary, only]]?

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Αβρααμ ὅτι Τὰς ἑπτὰ ἀμνάδας ταύτας λήμψῃ παρʼ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα ὦσίν μοι εἰς μαρτύριον ὅτι ἐγὼ ὤρυξα τὸ φρέαρ τοῦτο.
hint: Take these seven lambs from me as a witness that I dug this well.

notes.text: μαρτύριον, one sense, *a testimony, proof*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves it out.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] the seven lambs [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[you will take|you will take, you will receive, you will take hold of and grasp and seize]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near]] me, [[that|that, in order that]] may be to me [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[a testimony|a testimony, a proof]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] I [[I dug|I dug, I dug up, I dug through and made a canal through, I buried]] [[the well|the well, the tank and cistern and reservoir, the oil jar]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]].

greek: διὰ τοῦτο ἐπωνόμασεν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου Φρέαρ ὁρκισμοῦ, ὅτι ἐκεῖ ὤμοσαν ἀμφότεροι.
hint: So the place is named Well of the oath, for there both swore.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēr šābaʿ*, Beersheba. The Greek translates the name, *Well of the administration of an oath*.
ὁρκισμός, one translation, *administration of an oath*: plain text.

reading: [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]] [[gave a surname|gave a surname, named, called, pronounced]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity]] [[of that|of that, of the one there, of the more remote]] [[name:Φρέαρ]] of administration of an oath, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[there|there, in that place]] [[swore|swore, swore to and affirmed and confirmed by oath, swore that one would, swore by]] [[each|each, both of two]].

names.gloss: (Φρέαρ, "a well", the first word of the name the verse gives the place, for Hebrew Bĕʾēr šebaʿ)

greek: καὶ διέθεντο διαθήκην ἐν τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου. ἀνέστη δὲ Αβιμελεχ καὶ Οχοζαθ ὁ νυμφαγωγὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ Φικολ ὁ ἀρχιστράτηγος τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν γῆν τῶν Φυλιστιιμ.
hint: They make a covenant at the well of the oath; Abimelech, Ahuzzath and Phicol return to the land of the Philistines.

notes.text: [[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, as at 21:22.
The article before a people's name is not printed, as at 10:16.
ἐπιστρέφω, the chain of GEN 8:12.

reading: and [[arranged as they liked|arranged as they liked, disposed of, disposed of their property and devised it by will, set out for sale and disposed of, arranged mutually, made a covenant with, settled with]] [[a disposition|a disposition of property by will, a will and testament, an arrangement between two parties, a covenant]] [[in the well|within, inside of, and by means of the well, the tank and cistern and reservoir, the oil jar]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath]]. [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβιμελεχ]] and [[name:Οχοζαθ]] the leader of the bride of him and [[name:Φικολ]] the commander-in-chief [[of the power|of the power, of the might, of the strength, of the ability, of the authority, of the force for war and forces, of the quantity, of the faculty and capacity, of the force and meaning, of the worth and value]] of him and [[turned about|turned about, turned round, returned, turned towards, corrected and made to repent]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]].

names.gloss: (Φυλιστιιμ, from Hebrew Pĕlištîm, the people of Pĕlešet)

greek: καὶ ἐφύτευσεν Αβρααμ ἄρουραν ἐπὶ τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο ἐκεῖ τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου Θεὸς αἰώνιος.
hint: Abraham plants a plot by the well of the oath and calls there on the name of the Lord, Everlasting God.

notes.lemma: ἄρουραν ἐπὶ τῷ φρέατι τοῦ ὅρκου
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾēšel bibʾēr šābaʿ*, *a tamarisk in Beersheba*. The Greek has ἄρουρα, *tilled land*, *at the well of the oath*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾēl ʿôlām*. The Greek has θεός, anarthrous, capitalised by Rahlfs as the name called on.
Middle Liddell is first *tilled* or *arable land*.
Capitalised because it is the name called upon, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[planted|planted, planted for himself, begot, produced and brought about and caused]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[tilled land|tilled land, arable land, seed-land, cornland, land and earth, a woman as bearing children, a measure of land]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near]] [[to the well|to the well, to the tank and cistern and reservoir, to the oil jar]] [[of the object by which one swears|of the object by which one swears, of the witness of an oath, of the oath]] and [[called upon|called upon, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper, was called by surname]] [[there|there, in that place]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]] [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind]] [[lasting for an age|lasting for an age, ever-lasting, eternal]].

greek: παρῴκησεν δὲ Αβρααμ ἐν τῇ γῇ τῶν Φυλιστιιμ ἡμέρας πολλάς.
hint: Abraham sojourns many days in the land of the Philistines.

notes.text: The accusative of extent, ἡμέρα and πολύς.

reading: [[dwelt beside|dwelt beside, dwelt along the coast of, lived near, dwelt among, lay near, lived in and sojourned]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[name:Φυλιστιιμ]] [[days|days, day-breaks, times]] [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long]].
